The lithium-ion batteries that power our smartphones are getting smaller but more powerful all the time.

In this case, those nanoparticles consist of iron oxide coated on top of nickel ferrite; both compounds contain oxygen atoms as well as metal ions like Fe2+ or Ni3+, which can be reduced during discharge into metallic forms such as zero-valent metals (Fe0) while being oxidized back again upon recharging through electrochemical reactions involving water molecules present within electrolyte solutions used inside these devices’ cells .

It also means less waste produced since only small amounts needed per unit area compared against traditional methods requiring large quantities raw material inputs before processing begins .

[NEWS] News from the world of science and technology. \NEWs\ 2018-03-14, by ANS (Astronomical Society)
The lithium-ion batteries that power our smartphones are getting smaller but more powerful all the time.
But there’s still room for improvement in how they work – especially when it comes to charging them up quickly without damaging their performance over many cycles.
Now researchers at MIT have come up with an entirely different approach: using nanoscale particles made out of two materials instead of just one.
In this case, those nanoparticles consist of iron oxide coated on top of nickel ferrite; both compounds contain oxygen atoms as well as metal ions like Fe2+ or Ni3+, which can be reduced during discharge into metallic forms such as zero-valent metals (Fe0) while being oxidized back again upon recharging through electrochemical reactions involving water molecules present within electrolyte solutions used inside these devices’ cells .
This process allows electrons flow freely between adjacent layers where each layer contains either positively charged cations (+ve charge carriers )or negatively ones (- ve). The result is higher energy density than conventional Li ion based systems due mainly because no additional components need added beyond what already exists naturally occurring minerals found abundantly throughout Earth's crust!
It also means less waste produced since only small amounts needed per unit area compared against traditional methods requiring large quantities raw material inputs before processing begins .

[NEWS] News from the world of science and technology. \NEWs\ 2018-03-14, by ANS (Astronomical Society)
The lithium-ion batteries that power our smartphones are getting smaller but more powerful all the time.
But there’s still room for improvement in how they work – especially when it comes to charging them up quickly without damaging their performance over many cycles.
Now researchers at MIT have come up with an entirely different approach: using nanoscale particles made out of two materials instead of just one.
In this case, those nanoparticles consist of iron oxide coated on top of nickel ferrite; both compounds contain oxygen atoms as well as metal ions like Fe2+ or Ni3+, which can be reduced during discharge into metallic forms such as zero-valent metals (Fe0) while being oxidized back again upon recharging through electrochemical reactions involving water molecules present within electrolyte solutions used inside these devices’ cells .
This process allows electrons flow freely between adjacent layers where each layer contains either positively charged cations (+ve charge carriers )or negatively ones (- ve). The result is higher energy density than conventional Li ion based systems due mainly because no additional components need added beyond what already exists naturally occurring minerals found abundantly throughout Earth's crust!
It also means less waste produced since only small amounts needed per unit area compared against traditional methods requiring large quantities raw material inputs before processing begins .

Also anything written or co-written with Neal Stephenson ("Cryptonomicon") including his latest novel about space travel called Seveneves"
And then there was that one movie where they were all trying to get back home from Mars... oh yeah! That was good too...
There have been so many great ones over time it would be hard to pick just
one. But here goes:
1.) Asimov’s “Foundation” trilogy – still my favourite SF ever read,
and probably will remain so forevermore;
2.) Heinlein’s “Stranger In A Strange Land”, which changed me when i first
read it at age fifteen…i’ve never looked upon life quite the same since…
3.) Clarke’s “2001:A Space Odyssey”; although he wrote several other fine novels,
this remains perhaps THE classic work of modern-day Sci-Fi literature…and yes,
the film version does justice to the original story line very well indeed.
4.) Herbert’s “DUNE”. This may seem like blasphemy coming from someone who loves
“FOUNDATION” above everything else…but after reading “STRANGER IN STRANGE LAND”
at such a young impressionable age…I think maybe Mr.Clarkes’ influence had more impact than any others combined….but nonetheless…”DUNE” stands alone among ALL works of literary merit within the genre…it IS truly unique…the only thing comparable might possibly be Frankenstein..
5.) Bradbury’s short stories collection entitled simply ”THE MARTIAN CHRONICLES”.
6.) Vonnegut’s Slaughterhouse Five..which actually isn’t strictly speaking ‘SciFi’
as much as it is social commentary wrapped up inside what appears initially to be pure fantasy…but once you start thinking about how relevant those themes become today…..well……you’ll see why i included him amongst these giants anyway :)
7.) Pohl’s Gateway Trilogy–although admittedly somewhat dated now compared to most recent offerings available nowadays…still holds true even though we know better things exist beyond our own solar system already thanks largely due to advances made during Apollo missions etcetera ad nauseum blahblahblablabla yaddayadaaaahhhhhh!!!!!!
8.) Zelazny’s Amber Chronicles Series—again another example wherein technology plays little role whatsoever yet somehow manages nevertheless convey profound insights into human nature through cleverly crafted allegories involving magic rather than machines per se …very interesting stuff indeed especially considering current events unfolding around us right NOW!!! :P
